items.claim: Every woe-particle claim in the row is byte-exact at the cited verses: the verse-initial onset at 22:13, the divine therefore-clause at 22:18, and the fourfold funeral cry with its two bare and two vav-prefixed forms in that one verse.
items.evidence: MT 22:13 opens verse-initially with the bare particle, ה֣וֹי בֹּנֶ֤ה (byte tier). MT 22:18 carries the therefore-clause in YHWH's own mouth, כֹּֽה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה (byte tier) -- the plain divine form, no tsevaot in that verse (byte-checked), so the frame owner is not in doubt. The same verse then carries exactly four further particles in two pairs, ה֥וֹי אָחִ֖י וְה֣וֹי אָח֑וֹת and ה֥וֹי אָד֖וֹן וְה֥וֹי הֹדֹֽה (both byte tier): two bare and two vav-prefixed, precisely as the row counts them, and the vav-prefixed pair is of a shape no bare-token sweep can see (sweep: 2 verses carry the vav-prefixed shape, MT keys). Parashah citations are all correct under the claimed type -- SAMEKH at MT 22:12, 22:17 and 22:19, with no other marked verse inside the span (sweep: 2 marked verses in 22:13-22:19, both SAMEKH) -- and no ketiv/qere note falls in the span (sweep: 0 notes over 22:13-22:19), so nothing is owed on that layer. Residual precision point, no boundary effect: the rationale's phrase 'two verse-initial bare-hoy onsets' carries its digit without the woe qualifier the row supplies elsewhere -- a role-blind sweep of the verse-initial bare particle returns 4 verses (sweep: 4 verses, MT keys -- 22:13, 23:1, 30:7, 47:6), and the digit 2 holds only for the woe-onset role, which the device note does name; the particles at 48:1 and 50:27 are byte-checked as mid-verse, so they cannot inflate the verse-initial figure either way. The unquoted close at 22:19 carries the ordinary defective Jerusalem spelling, so no plene claim is at stake.

items.claim: The span closes on MT 22:23, one of the twelve doubled ketiv/qere verses, with no variant disclosure anywhere in the row and an unqualified span-wide null asserted in its place -- and the two notes sit on the very feminine-singular forms the row's addressee-shift warrant rests on.
items.evidence: MT 22:23 carries two ketiv/qere notes, and the source bytes show both readings standing inline: ישבתי יֹשַׁבְתְּ֙ and מקננתי מְקֻנַּ֖נְתְּ (byte tier) -- in each pair the unpointed ketiv carries the archaic final-yod second-feminine-singular ending that the pointed qere drops. That is exactly the grammatical feature the row's boundary turns on, since its stated ground is a shift to 'a feminine-singular you answering for her own history', and its closing evidence is the English rendering of that same verse. The row's only disclosure surface states that no mark falls within 22:20-22:23: true for the parashah layer (byte-checked -- no PE or SAMEKH at MT 22:20-22:23, and the SAMEKH at MT 22:19 is correctly cited), but stated without qualification it reads as a span-wide null over a verse in the book's largest variant inventory and in its flagged doubled-note group. The declared false-positive disposition of this same finding does not hold: the verse is inside the span, not adjacent to it; the notes are two, not one; and they land on the row's own warrant rather than on incidental material. The boundary itself survives untouched -- MT 22:20's opening imperatives are byte-clean and carry no variant note, עֲלִ֤י הַלְּבָנוֹן֙ וּֽצְעָ֔קִי (byte tier), with second-feminine-singular suffixes running on through 22:21-22:22 -- so this challenges the disclosure and the unengaged variant, not the seam.

items.claim: The oath opener, the repeated Coniah name form, the closing divine frame and every mark citation are byte-exact; only the onomastic label 'throne-name' goes beyond what the bytes carry.
items.evidence: MT 22:24 opens with the oath and its divine attribution, חַי אָנִי֮ נְאֻם יְהוָה֒ (byte tier), and names the king כָּנְיָ֤הוּ (byte tier); MT 22:28 names him again, כָּנְיָ֔הוּ (byte tier). The two are the identical consonantal form at both sites (skeleton כניהו; sweep: 3 verses carry this name-form token, MT keys -- 22:24, 22:28, 37:1), differing only in accentuation, so the row's 'repeating the same name' is exact, and holding this form apart from the Jeconiah and Jehoiachin forms used elsewhere is the correct three-form split for this one king. The declared closing frame is really there and is in YHWH's own mouth, not a quoted prophet's: MT 22:30 opens כֹּ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה (byte tier, no tsevaot in that verse, byte-checked); the summons the row cites is likewise byte-true, MT 22:29 שִׁמְעִ֖י דְּבַר יְהוָֽה (byte tier). Mark citations are correct under type and complete for the span: no PE or SAMEKH at MT 22:23, SAMEKH at MT 22:27 and 22:29, none at 22:30 (sweep: 2 marked verses in 22:24-22:30), and no ketiv/qere note falls there (sweep: 0 notes over 22:24-22:30). Two residuals, neither touching the boundary: 'throne-name' is an onomastic reading the bytes do not carry -- nothing in the source designates any of the three forms as such, and if any form is usually read that way it is the longer one, so the label is the kind of unverifiable claim this book's discipline holds rather than asserts. And the neighbor note that no mark falls on 22:23 is true for the parashah layer only, since that verse carries two ketiv/qere notes -- though 22:23 lies outside this span, so no span disclosure is owed from here.

items.claim: The single-unit reading is argued in a device vocabulary that cannot register the one recurrent macro-onset formula standing twice inside the span -- verse-initially at MT 23:5 and in its lachen shape at MT 23:7, each immediately after a setumah the row itself discloses -- while the rejected alternative tests a split point that has no such support.
items.evidence: MT 23:5 opens verse-initially הִנֵּ֨ה יָמִ֤ים בָּאִים֙ נְאֻם יְהוָ֔ה and MT 23:7 opens לָכֵ֛ן הִנֵּֽה יָמִ֥ים בָּאִ֖ים נְאֻם יְהוָ֑ה (both byte tier). This is a book-wide recurrent onset, not local colour: sweep 15 verses carry the formula (MT keys), and 14 of the 15 are verse-initial -- 6 in the bare shape, 8 in the lachen-prefixed shape; one of the fifteen sits inside the book's single renumbering zone (oshb:Jer.9.24 = web:Jer.9.25), so the digit names its numbering space. Both in-span onsets fall immediately after the two setumahs the row does disclose (MT 23:4 and 23:6), so the mark layer and the formula layer coincide at the same two points; but the row's cohesion test is worded as 'no addressee, scene, or discourse-imperative seam', which is a vocabulary in which neither point can appear, and the rejected alternative instead tests 23:3, where the onset formula is byte-absent and no mark stands (sweep: 3 marked verses in 23:1-23:8 -- MT 23:4, 23:6, 23:8 -- none of them at 23:3). A further byte fact at the row's own close goes undisclosed: MT 23:7-23:8 is a near-twin of MT 16:14-16:15 -- the pair shares an identical seven-word consonantal opening, לכן הנה ימים באים נאם יהוה ולא (skeleton tier), and an identical sixteen-word consonantal run after it, diverging only at the verb inflection and from the added clause onward -- so the closing pair reads as a recurring block carrying its own header rather than as the terminus of one sustained speech. Separately, the name at MT 23:6 that the row calls a throne-name and uses to close the promise is quoted in English only, with no pointed splice, in a span where divine-name objects are distinct and must be named before they are counted; no digit is claimed, so this is engagement short of the standard rather than a false count.

items.claim: The row's cohesion warrant -- one continuous first-person indictment opened at 23:9 -- blends two different first-person speakers, and the speaker change inside the span satisfies the row's own opening-seam test at a second point it never engages.
items.evidence: At MT 23:9 the first person is the prophet's, and the bytes settle it: נִשְׁבַּ֧ר לִבִּ֣י בְקִרְבִּ֗י with YHWH standing in the third person a few clauses later, מִפְּנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה (both byte tier). That is precisely the ground the row uses to open the unit -- the prophet's own voice replacing the direct divine voice. From MT 23:11 onward the first person is YHWH's, byte-marked inside the same clause: גַּם בְּבֵיתִ֛י מָצָ֥אתִי רָעָתָ֖ם נְאֻם יְהוָֽה (byte tier), and again at MT 23:12, כִּֽי אָבִ֨יא עֲלֵיהֶ֥ם רָעָ֛ה ... with the postpositive divine formula closing that verse too (byte tier); the divine first person then carries 23:13-23:14 and the sentence at 23:15. So the row's own criterion -- whose first person is speaking -- is met a second time at 23:11, inside the span, and 'the same first-person indictment opened at Jer.23.9' is a blended speech-role claim of exactly the class this book's frame-ownership discipline forbids: the mouth is named at the seam and then left unnamed across the body. What the row gets right is not in dispute: the opener is byte-clean and verse-initial in its defective spelling, MT 23:9 לַנְּבִאִ֞ים (byte tier); the mark citations are correct under type and complete (SAMEKH at MT 23:8, 23:13, 23:14; PE at MT 23:15, correctly not conflated with the setumahs; sweep: 3 marked verses in the span); and no ketiv/qere note falls there (sweep: 0 notes over 23:9-23:15). The boundary stands; the warrant does not.

items.claim: The row's own splice shows the opening verse is carried by a verse-initial koh-amar-tsevaot frame, yet the row labels the opener a discourse-frame imperative, never names whose mouth carries the formula, and omits the frame from its declared signals -- while excusing the next seam for lacking exactly that marker.
items.evidence: MT 23:16 opens verse-initially כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֗וֹת (byte tier), and the imperative the row names, אַֽל תִּשְׁמְע֞וּ (byte tier), follows the frame rather than opening the verse; the row splices the whole run at byte tier and then describes it only as a discourse-frame imperative, and its English quotation begins after the frame clause the verse actually opens with. The frame is a first-order object in this book, not background: sweep 50 verses carry the tsevaot form of the formula (MT keys), 21 of them verse-initial, MT 23:16 among them -- and MT 28:2 sits in that same verse-initial set with the identical shape in the false prophet Hananiah's mouth, which is why naming the speaker here is not pedantry. At 23:16 the mouth is YHWH's, reported by the prophet; the row never says so, and the koh-amar frame contained in its own Hebrew evidence is absent from its declared signal list, which carries only the imperative and the addressee shift. The mismatch compounds in the rejected alternative, which excuses the following seam as opening 'even without a formal imperative or koh-amar marker' while the koh-amar marker standing at this row's own opening has been left unnamed. Everything else checks: MT 23:18 carries the span's only variant note (sweep: 1 note over 1 verse in MT 23:16-23:22), the row discloses it and correctly declines to splice from that verse -- the unpointed ketiv stands beside the pointed qere in the source bytes, דברי דְּבָר֖וֹ (byte tier) -- and PE at MT 23:15 with SAMEKH at MT 23:18 and 23:22 are correct under their types. The boundary is right, and on the bytes better supported than the row claims.

items.claim: The noun-versus-verb hazard at 23:31 is handled exactly as the bytes require -- both shapes spliced at byte tier from the one verse, with a correct book-wide digit -- and the plene/defective divergence between the prophet-nouns at 23:30 and 23:31 is carried through the splices per attested spelling.
items.evidence: MT 23:31 carries the formula noun with the divine name, הִנְנִ֥י עַל הַנְּבִיאִ֖ם נְאֻם יְהוָ֑ה (byte tier), and then the finite verb governing its own cognate noun with no divine name following it, הַלֹּקְחִ֣ים לְשׁוֹנָ֔ם וַֽיִּנְאֲמ֖וּ נְאֻֽם (byte tier). The row's reading of the second as verb-plus-cognate-noun standing outside the formula is what the bytes carry, and its digit is exact: that verb form occurs in 1 verse book-wide (sweep: 1 verse, MT keys), so a role-blind token count at this verse would indeed fold the formula noun and the verbal pair into one tally. The row also preserved, without remarking on it, the spelling divergence between MT 23:30 הַנְּבִאִ֖ים and MT 23:31 הַנְּבִיאִ֖ם (byte tier at each site) -- sweeps and splices per attested spelling, which is the discipline this book demands. Mark citations are correct under type and complete (SAMEKH at MT 23:22 and 23:29; none at MT 23:30-23:32), and no ketiv/qere note falls there (sweep: 1 marked verse and 0 notes over 23:23-23:32). Two residual precision points, neither moving the boundary: the third member of the refrain does not repeat the quoted string, since MT 23:32 reads הִ֠נְנִי עַֽל נִבְּאֵ֞י חֲלֹמ֥וֹת שֶׁ֨קֶר֙ (byte tier) -- a construct participle with a different object rather than 'against the prophets' -- and it is the one member the row leaves unspliced; and the lachen that opens the quoted MT 23:30 run, לָכֵ֛ן הִנְנִ֥י עַל הַנְּבִאִ֖ים (byte tier), does not recur at 23:31 or 23:32, so what actually stands three times is the shorter presentative-plus-preposition shape the row glosses, not the full quoted clause.

items.claim: The unit's defining device -- the burden/oracle wordplay that supplies the row's literature type and its whole cohesion argument -- is asserted in English only with no pointed splice, the English witness the row does quote never carries the 'burden' sense at all, and the byte-level pun that closes the unit at 23:39 goes unengaged.
items.evidence: The row splices its opening conditional at byte tier but never quotes the word its argument is about, though the bytes carry it twice in that same opening verse: MT 23:33 מַה מַשָּׂ֖א יְהוָ֑ה and אֶת מַה מַשָּׂ֔א (both byte tier). The omission bites harder than usual because the English rendering the row quotes never uses 'burden' anywhere in 23:33-23:40 -- it renders the noun as 'message' throughout -- so the double sense the row asserts has no witness in the row's own evidence and can stand only on the Hebrew that is not supplied (sweep: 0 occurrences of the burden word and 8 of the message word across those eight verses in the English witness). The token is also hazardous in a direction the row does not disclose: the bare token stands in 7 verses (sweep: 7 verses, MT keys), four of them the sabbath-load material of ch 17 and only three inside this span, because both prefixed forms at MT 23:36 are invisible to a bare-token sweep. Third, the unit's own closing device is unengaged: MT 23:39 reads וְנָשִׁ֥יתִי אֶתְכֶ֖ם נָשֹׁ֑א (byte tier), where the infinitive absolute carries the consonantal skeleton נשא -- the same three consonants as the noun the whole unit turns on (sweep: 2 verses carry that bare token, MT keys) -- so the sentence the row describes only as one 'of forgetting' is where the wordplay resolves at byte level. Finally the continuity claim resting on 23:38 quotes no frame form and the frame is absent from the declared signals: MT 23:38 does carry לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה (byte tier, YHWH's own mouth, no tsevaot in that verse), so the claim is true but unevidenced. The one mark in the span is correctly cited (SAMEKH at MT 23:40, the chapter's close) and no ketiv/qere note falls there (sweep: 1 marked verse and 0 notes over 23:33-23:40).
